title: Mobility Officer
raw_text:
8-882A. Military Occupational Specialty 882A—Mobility Officer
   a. Licensing/certification requirement. None.
   b. Prerequisites. AR 56-9 and DA Cir 601 series.
   c. MOS 882A. MOS 882A is an accession MOS. The enlisted feeder MOS is 88N.
   d. Associated SQI.
        (1) 0--No special qualifications.
        (2) 8--Instructor.
        (3) P--Parachutist.
        (4) T--Transition (personnel only).
        (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
   e. Associated ASI. (Note: Refer to table 6-6 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all
MOS)).
   f. Qualifications.
        (1) WO1/CW2 must--
              (a) Complete the Warrant Officer Basic Course.
              (b) Have a physical profile of not less than 222221, per AR 40-501.
              (c) Have a distance visual acuity, which corrects to at least 20/20 in one eye, and
20/40 in the other eye.
              (d) Have normal color vision based on no more than four errors in reading the pseudo
isochromatic plates test.
              (e) A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) - 0120 cm, seated Power
Throw (PT) - 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) - 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) - 0036
shuttles.
              (f) Be a U.S. citizen. Qualify for a security eligibility of SECRET.
        (2) CW3 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (1).
              (b) Complete the Transportation Warrant Officer Advanced Course.
              (c) Qualify for a security eligibility of TOP SECRET.
        (3) CW4 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (2).
              (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Staff Course (WOSC).
        (4) CW5 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (3).
              (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Senior Staff Course
(WOSSC).
   g. Duties.
        (1) W01/02—
              (a) Directs and coordinates the implementation of Global Transportation Network
(GTN), Department of the Army Movement Management System-Redesign (DASMMS-R),
Automated Command and Control Information System (ACCIS), ACCIS-Air-Load Module (ALM),
Automated Information Management System (AIMS-II), Automated Air Load Planning System
(AALPS), Air Movement Flow Table (AMFT), Computer Aided Loading and Manifesting System
(CALM), Movement Tracking System (MTS), Computerized Movement Planning and Status
System (COMPASS), LOGMAR/BARCODE scanners, Combat Service Support System
(CSSCS), Worldwide Port System (WPS), Frequency Tag System, Mobile Subscriber equipment
(MSE) and Tactical Terminal Adapters (TTA).
              (b) Plans, assesses, supervises and reports convoy and cargo handling operations at
company, battalion, brigade of division level.
              (c) Plans movement of personnel, unit equipment and port call.
              (d) Facilitates international movement by rail, highway, air and water to, within and
from the theater assigned.
              (e) Coordinates transportation plans.
              (f) Prepares, supervises and coordinates cargo handling, ensuring its compliance
with U.S. Army, contracted and host nation regulatory requirement.
              (g) Seaport operations, marshaling equipment, inspection standards for sealift,
theater opening procedures.
               (h) Schedules movements within a theater of operations.
              (i) Plans intra and inter theater movement by any mode of transportation.
         (2) CW3—
              (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g (1).
              (b) Directs and coordinates the implementation of the Joint Operations Planning and
Executing System (JOPES), Movement Planning Module (MPM), Improved Computerized
Deployment System (ICODES) and Automated System for Processing Unit Requirements
(ASPUR).
              (c) Identifies the capabilities and limitations of the host nation transportation
infrastructure.
              (d) Recommends location of checkpoints along main and alternate supply routes.
              (e) Supports development of OPLAN/OPS orders.
              (f) Assesses unit transportation capabilities to support proposed operations.
              (g) Assesses and incorporates non-programmed movements into the movement
plan.
         (3) CW4—
              (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g (2).
              (b) Directs and coordinates the implementation of the Army Mobilization and
Operations Planning Execution System (AMOPES).
              (c) Reviews ocean cargo manifests and manifest recapitulation.
         (4) CW5—
              (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g (3).
              (b) Performs as technical advisor to higher echelons of command and allied armies
on transportation matters.
    h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
         (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate (Gold).
         (2) Table 8-882-1. Physical requirements.
         (3) The following grades are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels:
W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3 equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are
listed in the following standards of grade tables:
              (a) Table 8-882A-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
              (b) Table 8-882A-3. Standards of grade TDA.

Plan, supervise, and review work of assigned subordinates.
(b) Plans, assesses, supervises and reports convoy and cargo handling operations at company, battalion, brigade of division level.
Plan work assignments and equipment allocations to meet transportation, operations or production goals.
(c) Plans movement of personnel, unit equipment and port call.
Coordinate or perform activities associated with shipping, receiving, distribution, or transportation.
(d) Facilitates international movement by rail, highway, air and water to, within and from the theater assigned.
Inspect loaded cargo, cargo lashed to decks or in storage facilities, and cargo handling devices to determine compliance with health and safety regulations and need for maintenance.

(g) Seaport operations, marshaling equipment, inspection standards for sealift, theater opening procedures.
Plan and establish schedules.

Coordinate implementation of computer system plan with establishment personnel and outside vendors.

Determine cargo transportation capabilities by reading documents that set forth cargo loading and securing procedures, capacities, and stability factors.
(c) Identifies the capabilities and limitations of the host nation transportation infrastructure.
Select shipment routes, based on nature of goods shipped, transit times, or security needs.
(d) Recommends location of checkpoints along main and alternate supply routes.
Receive or prepare work orders.
(e) Supports development of OPLAN/OPS orders.
Provide logistical facility or capacity planning analyses for distribution or transportation functions.
(f) Assesses unit transportation capabilities to support proposed operations.
Develop program plans for individuals or assist in plan development.
(g) Assesses and incorporates non-programmed movements into the movement plan.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
